reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown split the sale in two: fifty silver shekels bought only the floor and oxen, while six hundred gold shekels later purchased the whole surrounding site.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen names this exact figure as his showcase instance of the Chronicler routinely inflating the sums it copies from Samuel-Kings.

quotes.text: "David gave to Araunah for his threshing-floor 600 shekels of gold ;" compare with 2Samuel xxiv. 24, 50 shekels of silver; to make the king pay right royally costs the Chronicler nothing.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Chronicler's inflation of the Samuel-Kings figures in this very passage.

sides.snippet: So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
sides.verseText: The king said to Araunah, No; but I will most assuredly buy it of you at a price. Neither will I offer burnt-offerings to Yahweh my God which cost me nothing. So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

sides.snippet: So David gave to Ornan for the place six hundred shekels of gold by weight.
sides.verseText: So David gave to Ornan for the place six hundred shekels of gold by weight.
